title: Start a project and import media
summary: Create a new project, bring in video clips and save.

steps.say: Press Control Alt N, or click New project on the Home screen, to start a project.

checks.prompt: Is the Import mode screen showing, with a Project name field at the top left and a media browser?

hints: The Home screen appears when Premiere starts. New project is a button near the top left.
If a project is already open, use the File menu, then New, then Project.
steps.why: Every edit lives inside a project, which remembers your media and timelines.

steps.say: Click Project name at the top left and type a name for your project.

check.prompt: Has the Project name field at the top left been changed from Untitled to a new name?

hints: The field reads Untitled until you change it. Click it and type.
Below the name, Project location lets you choose the folder for the project file.
steps.why: A clear name helps you find the project later.

steps.say: In the browser on the left, open a folder, then tick the clips you want to use.

check.prompt: Are one or more clip thumbnails ticked, with a selection tray showing them at the bottom?

hints: Each thumbnail has a checkbox in its corner. Ticked clips appear in the tray along the bottom.
Your Videos folder and Desktop are listed on the left under Local.
steps.why: Ticked clips are imported and placed in a new sequence for you.

steps.say: Click Create at the bottom right.

checks.prompt: Is the Edit workspace open with the clips in the Project panel and a sequence in the Timeline?

hints: Create is the blue button in the lower right corner of the Import screen.
If Create is greyed out, give the project a name first.
steps.why: Creating the project opens the editing workspace with your clips ready.

steps.say: Look at the Project panel at the bottom left and check your clips are listed.

checks.prompt: Are clip names or thumbnails visible in the Project panel at the bottom left?

hints: The Project panel tab shows the project name. Click it if another tab is in front.
Switch between list and thumbnail view with the small icons at the bottom of the panel.
steps.why: The Project panel is your library; everything you edit comes from here.

steps.say: To add more files later, press Control I and choose them.

checks.prompt: Is an Import file window open?

hints: Click Cancel in the window if you have nothing else to add right now.
You can also drag files from File Explorer straight into the Project panel.
steps.why: Control I works at any time, not only when the project is created.

steps.say: Press Control S to save the project.
hints: Close the Import window first if it is still open, then press Control S.
You can also use the File menu, then Save.
steps.why: Saving records your work in the project file.
